title: Module Header and Imports
content: The file opens with a documentation block summarising the 8 key results proved here, then imports Mathlib (the full Lean 4 mathematical library) and the companion file `Erdos622Problem`, which supplies the definitions `IsErdosFaudreeGraph`, `IsRegular`, and `vertexCount`. The namespace `Erdos622OQ04` and the section variables — an arbitrary `Fintype` with `DecidableEq` — set up the polymorphic graph universe for all subsequent theorems.
mathContext: All theorems are stated over an abstract finite vertex type $V$ with decidable equality, so they apply to any concrete finite graph. `SimpleGraph V` is Mathlib's undirected, loop-free, simple graph structure on $V$.

title: Handshaking Lemma for Regular Graphs
content: Proves `regular_edge_count`: in a $d$-regular graph, $2|E| = |V| \cdot d$. The proof chains Mathlib's `sum_degrees_eq_twice_card_edges` (which states $\sum_v \deg(v) = 2|E|$) with a `calc` block that collapses the degree sum to $|V| \cdot d$ using regularity, then applies `omega` to close the arithmetic. This is the digital handshaking lemma — every edge contributes exactly one to each endpoint's degree count, so summing all degrees double-counts edges.
mathContext: $\sum_{v \in V} \deg(v) = 2|E|$ because each edge $\{u, v\}$ contributes $1$ to $\deg(u)$ and $1$ to $\deg(v)$. When $G$ is $d$-regular, $\sum_v \deg(v) = |V| \cdot d$, giving $2|E| = |V| \cdot d$.

title: Edge Count in Erdős-Faudree Graphs
content: The corollary `erdos_faudree_edge_count` instantiates the handshaking lemma for EF graphs ($2n$ vertices, $(n+1)$-regular). After unfolding `IsErdosFaudreeGraph` to extract $|V| = 2n$, substituting into the handshaking result gives $2|E| = 2n(n+1)$, so $|E| = n(n+1)$. The proof delegate `omega` handles the linear arithmetic after the rewrite.
mathContext: For $G$ an Erdős-Faudree graph: $|V| = 2n$, $d = n+1$. By the handshaking lemma $2|E| = 2n(n+1)$, so $|E| = n(n+1) = \binom{n+1}{2} \cdot 2 / (n) \cdot n$. Numerically: $n = 3 \Rightarrow |E| = 12$; $n = 10 \Rightarrow |E| = 110$.

title: Inclusion-Exclusion Bound on Common Neighborhoods
content: Proves `common_neighbors_ge`: in a $d$-regular graph, $|N(u) \cap N(v)| + |V| \geq 2d$ for every pair $u, v$. The argument is a direct application of inclusion-exclusion: $|N(u) \cup N(v)| \leq |V|$ (neighborhoods are subsets of vertices) and $|N(u) \cup N(v)| = |N(u)| + |N(v)| - |N(u) \cap N(v)| = 2d - |N(u) \cap N(v)|$. Combining: $2d - |N(u) \cap N(v)| \leq |V|$. Mathlib's `card_union_add_card_inter` encodes the inclusion-exclusion identity, and `omega` closes the inequality arithmetic.
mathContext: Inclusion-exclusion: $|A \cup B| = |A| + |B| - |A \cap B|$. Applied to neighbor sets: $|N(u) \cup N(v)| = 2d - |N(u) \cap N(v)|$. Since $N(u) \cup N(v) \subseteq V$, we get $|N(u) \cap N(v)| \geq 2d - |V|$, i.e., $|N(u) \cap N(v)| + |V| \geq 2d$.

title: Erdős-Faudree Graph: ≥2 Common Neighbors
content: The theorem `erdos_faudree_common_ge_two` is the quantitative heart of the absorbing method for EF graphs. It instantiates `common_neighbors_ge` with $d = n+1$ and $|V| = 2n$: the bound becomes $|N(u) \cap N(v)| + 2n \geq 2(n+1) = 2n+2$, so $|N(u) \cap N(v)| \geq 2$. This is tight: two is the minimum possible common neighborhood size given the graph parameters, and the absorbing method exploits this minimum to guarantee triangles exist.
mathContext: For EF graph: $2d - |V| = 2(n+1) - 2n = 2$. Hence every pair of vertices shares $\geq 2$ common neighbors. The positivity hypothesis $0 < n$ ensures $|V| = 2n \geq 2$, ruling out the degenerate $n = 0$ case.

title: Absorbing Triple and Absorbing Pairs
content: Defines the two core objects of the absorbing method. An `IsAbsorbingTriple G u v w` is a triangle $\{u, v, w\}$ where the edge $u$–$v$ is adjacent to $w$ through both endpoints ($u \sim w$ and $v \sim w$). The idea: if a Hamiltonian path uses the edge $u$–$v$, replacing it by $u$–$w$–$v$ 'absorbs' the isolated vertex $w$ into the path. `absorbingPairs G w` collects all ordered pairs $(u, v)$ for which such a triple exists — it is `noncomputable` because `Finset.filter` over the full product is not definitionally computable from the adjacency predicate.
mathContext:
Formally: $	ext{IsAbsorbingTriple}(u, v, w) \iff u \sim v \land u \sim w \land w \sim v \land u 
eq v \land u 
eq w \land v 
eq w$. The set $	ext{absorbingPairs}(w) = \{(u,v) \mid 	ext{IsAbsorbingTriple}(u,v,w)\}$ has size $\geq n$ (proved below).

title: Absorbing Triple Symmetry and Neighbor Lemmas
content: Two auxiliary lemmas establish basic structural properties. `isAbsorbingTriple_symm` shows that swapping the endpoint pair $(u,v) \mapsto (v,u)$ preserves the absorbing property — since adjacency is symmetric in simple graphs. `absorbingTriple_are_neighbors` recovers from an absorbing triple that both $u$ and $v$ are neighbors of the absorbed vertex $w$; this is an immediate consequence of the definition but needs to be stated for use in the density proof. The private lemma `mem_absorbingPairs` provides a propositional interface to the set membership condition.
mathContext: Symmetry: if $\text{IsAbsorbingTriple}(u,v,w)$ then $\text{IsAbsorbingTriple}(v,u,w)$, because $G.Adj$ is symmetric ($u \sim v \iff v \sim u$ in a SimpleGraph). The neighbor fact $u \sim w \land v \sim w$ follows from $h.2.1$ and $G.symm(h.2.2.1)$.

title: Triangle Existence in Dense Regular Graphs
content: Proves `absorbing_pair_exists`: if $G$ is $d$-regular with $|V| + 2 \leq 2d$, every vertex $w$ lies in a triangle. The proof is existential: pick any $u \in N(w)$ (possible since $|N(w)| = d \geq 3$), then apply `common_neighbors_ge` to get $|N(u) \cap N(w)| \geq 2d - |V| \geq 2 > 0$, so pick $v \in N(u) \cap N(w)$. The triple $(u, v, w)$ is then assembled by threading adjacency facts through `mem_neighborFinset`. The proof demonstrates how a density condition (large common neighborhood) automatically forces triangle existence.
mathContext: Hypothesis: $|V| + 2 \leq 2d$, equivalently $2d - |V| \geq 2$. Since $|N(u) \cap N(w)| \geq 2d - |V| \geq 2 > 0$ (by `common_neighbors_ge`), the intersection $N(u) \cap N(w)$ is nonempty, providing the third vertex $v$ of the triangle $u$-$v$-$w$.

title: Absorbing Pair Density: ≥n Pairs per Vertex
content: The central density theorem `erdos_faudree_absorbing_pairs_ge`: in an EF graph, every vertex $w$ has at least $n$ absorbing pairs. The proof is an injection argument — one of the most natural ways to establish cardinality lower bounds in combinatorics. Define $S = N(w) \setminus \{u_0\}$ (size $n$) and the map $f(u) = (u, v(u))$ where $v(u)$ is a chosen common neighbor of $u$ and $w$. Since first coordinates of $f(u)$ and $f(u')$ are $u$ and $u'$, injectivity is trivial. The final `calc` chains the inequality: $n = |S| = |f(S)| \leq |\text{absorbingPairs}(w)|$. The use of `Finset.card_pos.mp` to convert cardinality bounds into nonemptiness (for `choose`) is idiomatic Lean/Mathlib.
mathContext: Injection argument: define $f: S \to \text{absorbingPairs}(w)$ by $f(u) = (u, v(u))$ with $v(u) \in N(u) \cap N(w)$. Injectivity: $f(u) = f(u') \Rightarrow (u, v(u)) = (u', v(u')) \Rightarrow u = u'$. Thus $n = |S| = |f(S)| \leq |\text{absorbingPairs}(w)|$.

title: Absorbing Lemma (Probabilistic Statement)
content: Defines `HasAbsorbingStructure G ε hε`: the existence of a short cycle $C$ (length at most $\lceil \varepsilon |V| \rceil$) such that for any small vertex set $T$ disjoint from $C$ with $|T| \leq \delta |V|$, the cycle $C$ can be extended to a cycle covering $C \cup T$. This is the formalization of the main technical lemma in the DKM 2025 proof of Erdős Problem #622. The proof that EF graphs satisfy this property uses a probabilistic argument: for each vertex $t \in T$ and each absorbing pair $(u,v)$ for $t$, a random path through $(u,v,t)$ is sampled; the density bound $\geq n$ absorbing pairs per vertex makes the probability that $t$ is not absorbed exponentially small, and a union bound over $T$ finishes the argument. This probabilistic step is beyond current Mathlib and is left as a definition only.
mathContext: For small $\varepsilon, \delta > 0$: $\exists C$ (cycle, $|C| \leq \lceil \varepsilon n \rceil$) such that $\forall T \subseteq V \setminus V(C)$, $|T| \leq \delta n$, $\exists C'$ with $V(C') = V(C) \cup T$. The key probabilistic ingredient: each absorbing pair $(u,v)$ for $w$ contributes $\Omega(1/n^2)$ probability that a random cycle through $(u,v)$ absorbs $w$, so with $\geq n$ pairs the probability of failing to absorb $w$ is $\leq e^{-\Omega(1/n)}$, and a union bound over $|T| \leq \delta n$ completes the argument.
